title: Click-Lock vs Glue-Down Vinyl Plank: Which Installation Is Better?
meta: Click-lock or glue-down vinyl plank in a Seattle home? An installer explains when floating wins, when glue is worth it, and Wills Flooring's $2.50 labor rate.
keywords: click lock vs glue down vinyl plank, floating vs glue down LVP, glue down vinyl plank pros and cons, vinyl plank installation Seattle, best way to install luxury vinyl plank

blocks.lead: For most Seattle houses and condos, click-lock (floating) vinyl plank is the better installation: faster, kinder to imperfect subfloors, easier to repair, and it does not lock you into adhesive forever. Glue-down earns its place in large open areas, rooms with rolling loads or heavy furniture, and below-grade slabs where you want a floor that cannot shift.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs both methods at $2.50 per sq ft labor with a 500 sq ft minimum. Glue-down adds adhesive and more subfloor prep, which we quote at the estimate.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks whether glue-down is "the professional way" and click-lock is "the DIY way." That framing is wrong. Both are professional systems, and we install both across Seattle every month. What matters is your subfloor, your room sizes, and whether anyone will ever need to lift a plank again. Here is how we decide on a Ballard bungalow versus a Capitol Hill condo versus a West Seattle basement.

items.title: Click-lock
items.text: Planks snap together at the edges and the whole floor floats over the subfloor as one connected sheet, held down by its own weight and the baseboards. Nothing is glued or nailed. A perimeter gap of about 1/4 inch lets the floor expand and contract.

items.title: Glue-down
items.text: A pressure-sensitive or hard-set adhesive is troweled onto the subfloor and each plank is set into it. The floor becomes part of the subfloor. No expansion gap is needed, so long runs and open plans need no transition strips.

items.title: How they feel
items.text: Glue-down feels solid and quiet, closer to tile. Click-lock over an attached pad feels slightly softer and can sound hollow if the subfloor has dips. On a flat subfloor most people cannot tell the difference in socks.

items.title: Fixing one plank
items.text: Click-lock: pull the baseboard, unclick back to the damaged plank, replace it, reassemble. Glue-down: heat the plank, cut it out, scrape adhesive, glue a new one. Both are doable, but click-lock is cleaner and we can often do it in an hour.

blocks.note: Labor is $2.50 per sq ft for either method. Glue-down adds adhesive cost and usually more floor prep, which is why total quotes for glue-down run higher.

blocks.text: What Seattle homes push you toward

items.html: 1920s Wallingford or Ballard bungalow. Old fir subfloors are rarely flat and often have a little bounce. Click-lock with a rigid SPC core and an attached pad bridges that better than glue, which would need a full skim coat first.

Capitol Hill or Queen Anne condo. HOAs care about impact noise. A click-lock plank with an IIC-rated attached pad, or a separate acoustic underlayment, usually satisfies the building. Glue-down over concrete transmits more sound unless you add an acoustic layer first.

West Seattle or Beacon Hill basement slab. Both methods work if the slab tests dry. If the moisture reading is borderline, click-lock over a 6 mil vapor barrier is the safer bet, because an adhesive failure means starting over.
Home office with a rolling chair or a piano. Glue-down. Constant rolling loads and point weight are the one residential case where a bonded floor clearly wins.
Open-plan main floor over 50 ft long. Glue-down avoids the T-molding a floating floor needs mid-room. If you hate transitions, this is the reason to glue.

blocks.text: When each method is the wrong choice

a.title: Click-lock is wrong if
items: The room takes constant rolling loads or a 600 lb safe
You want zero transitions across a huge open plan
The product is a thin flexible LVP with no locking system
The subfloor has dips deeper than 3/16 in that will not be leveled

b.title: Glue-down is wrong if
items: The concrete slab has not passed a moisture test
You are installing over existing vinyl, tile or old hardwood
The subfloor is old fir with movement or gaps
You may want the floor out again in a few years, as in a rental

blocks.title: One thing nobody mentions:
blocks.text: Glue-down over existing sheet vinyl in a pre-1980 Seattle house is a bad idea twice over. The adhesive bond to old vinyl is unreliable, and disturbing old sheet vinyl or its backing can release asbestos. Float over it if it is flat and intact, or have it tested and abated before anything is glued.
What to ask before you sign either quote

items: Which method are you quoting, and why for my subfloor? A good answer names the subfloor material and its flatness.
What is the expansion gap plan, and where will transitions land? Ask to see them marked on a sketch.
For glue-down: which adhesive, what is the slab moisture reading, and how long before furniture can go back?
For click-lock: does the plank have an attached pad, or is a separate underlayment included in the quote?
Is subfloor prep a line item or an allowance? At Wills it is checked at the estimate and written into the firm quote, not discovered on install day.
Who handles the old floor? Tear-out and haul-away are quoted separately at our free estimate, and the answer changes if we can float over what is there.

faq.q: Is glue-down vinyl plank more durable than click-lock?
faq.a: The plank itself is the same; durability comes from the wear layer, not the installation method. Glue-down holds up better under rolling chairs and very heavy furniture because nothing can shift. In a normal Seattle living room or bedroom, a rigid-core click-lock floor lasts just as long.

faq.q: Does Wills Flooring charge more for glue-down installation?
faq.a: Labor is $2.50 per sq ft for either method, with a 500 sq ft minimum and $100 per stair. Glue-down quotes usually come out higher because adhesive is a separate material cost and the subfloor typically needs more prep to be smooth enough for a bonded floor.

faq.q: Can click-lock vinyl plank go over my old Seattle hardwood?
faq.a: Yes, if the hardwood is flat and solidly fastened. We float the plank over it with the appropriate underlayment. Glue-down over hardwood is not recommended because the wood moves seasonally and can break the adhesive bond, and you also lose the option of uncovering the hardwood later.

faq.q: Which is better for a Seattle condo with sound rules?
faq.a: Usually click-lock with an acoustic attached pad or a separate underlayment rated for impact noise. Many buildings in Capitol Hill and Belltown require an IIC rating in writing. Glue-down over concrete can meet it too, but only with an acoustic layer under the adhesive, which adds cost.

faq.q: How soon can I walk on a glue-down floor?
faq.a: Light foot traffic is fine after 24 hours with most pressure-sensitive adhesives, and furniture can go back after 48 to 72 hours. Click-lock is walkable the moment we finish and can take furniture the same day, which matters when you are living in the house during the work.

faq.q: Is loose-lay vinyl a third option?
faq.a: It exists, but we rarely recommend it for full rooms. Loose-lay planks rely on a heavy friction backing and perimeter adhesive, and they can creep in sunny south-facing Seattle rooms. It works for small utility spaces where quick removal matters more than a permanent look.
